description: The invariant the geography-split work (#192, plans/simapro-row-preparation.md) is judged on: a row whose name carries a place must keep reaching the flow it reaches today once the place is read off at load. One representative row per route a coded row lands by -- registry number, water material, land class, base-label match -- each selected by uuid because the recorded name is exactly what the change changes, and each claiming the target and the basis, so a split that moved a row would fail here and a split that only renamed would not. Plus the guard row: Particulates, SPM is code-shaped and is not a place, and stays whatever the whitelist gains. Every claim holds on the build of 1 September 2026 (run c5445e95) and must go on holding through every phase.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's Phosphorus, CN reaches Phosphorus by its number, code or no code on the name
expectations.comment: The number places it today with the code still on the name, and will go on placing it when the name arrives split. Selected by uuid: the recorded name is the one thing the split changes.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's Water, AE keeps reaching ocean water by its material
expectations.comment: The material table is keyed on the uuid, so the split cannot move it -- which is precisely what this claim is here to prove.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's Water, RME -- a custom geography, not an ISO code -- keeps its material route
expectations.comment: RME is the vendor's own Middle East grouping, glossed on the row. Phase 2 admits it beside RER and RAF; before and after, the row lands by its material.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's Occupation, annual crop, TH keeps reaching Cropland by its land class
expectations.comment: The class table is keyed on the uuid; #363 whitelisted this base for the lookup and the class placed the row regardless, which is half of how #192 was found.

expectations.title: AGRIBALYSE's Nitrogen oxides, CN reaches Nitrogen Oxides on a label, before and after the split
expectations.comment: Today the label is the synonym #364 wrote; after phase 2 it is the split base name itself, and the synonym is deleted. `basis: label` is the same either way, deliberately: the claim survives the mechanism swap and fails only if the row stops reaching the substance.

expectations.title: Particulates, SPM stays exactly as the vendor wrote it, code-shaped tail and all
expectations.comment: SPM parses as a code and is suspended particulate matter -- even a valid ISO alpha-3, for Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon. What this claim pins is that no widened whitelist ever reads a place off it. Rewritten on 2 September 2026, keeping the id, when #196 settled the row: it is read as the size-unstated total by the curated size table, which is a reading of the whole name and could not be made of a name the splitter had shortened.
